examples.shown_as: a public crowd sends a deposit arrow into the bank and two market labels send equity and debt arrows; the bank lends on to a person; then the return loop above is crossed with a red X, a red FAIL seal stamps the bank, and a long dotted curve swoops from the loan's RISK label to the boxed 'credit risk' entry in the sidebar

examples.idea: pay more for a bond and its fixed interest is a smaller share of what you paid, so its yield falls
examples.shown_as: the certificate steps down the chain of grey boxes, one owner at a time, its '500 every year' tag riding along; at each stop a new buyer logo and the price paid appear beside it (9K, then 15K, then 5K) and a red yield figure is written next to the price (5.5% at 9K, 3.3% at 15K)

examples.idea: because people buy differently, one basket cannot fit everyone, so consumers are split into similar groups
examples.shown_as: the consumption-data cylinder points to a heap of dark person silhouettes topped by a red India map; a callout from the heap opens a 'different consumption pattern' box (basket size and items vary; choice and purchasing power), then a down-arrow chain runs from 'socio-economic differentiation' to 'to tackle this' to 'homogeneous groups' and lights up the word SEGMENTATION

examples.idea: these indices decide real money: allowances for employees and minimum wages for labourers
examples.shown_as: the segmentation scene shrinks to a row with a '?' by the crowd; under CPI-UNME a down-arrow drops a green cash-wallet labelled dearness allowance with a cost-of-living strip, and the same happens under CPI-IW; callouts say whose pay each one adjusts; then CPI-AL and CPI-RL send two slanted arrows into one handshake-over-cash icon labelled minimum wage for farm and rural unskilled workers

examples.idea: The unbanked share became a national priority: financial inclusion.
examples.shown_as: the unshaded right part of the crowd is capped by a dark-red dome (the unbanked); a line runs from the dome to a photo of the then finance minister with a pink quote box; key words get a blue underline, and a 'priority: financial inclusion' tag points at the map

examples.idea: Old bank types could not serve the poor: too costly to reach, too expensive to use, wrong products.
examples.shown_as: the canvas resets to a yellow report tag with the RBI mark and a document icon over a beige shelf of the three existing bank types; a heading asks why they cannot reach the micro-finance segment and three pink reason boxes stack down one by one

examples.idea: if people grow faster than GDP, each person gets less, so GDP growth alone is not economic growth
examples.shown_as: two points on the rising GDP line get value tags (10 lakh, 50 lakh); red drop-lines fall from them to population labels (1,000 then 10,000); a yellow per-capita band fills in 1,000 under the first and 500 under the second; a grey box covers the stretch with a green 'GDP up' tag and a red 'per-capita down' tag; finally the 'economic growth' title turns pink and gets a red cross

examples.idea: growth's gains can stop at the government and miss people if they are not spent on health and education
examples.shown_as: the growth chart shrinks into a framed card; an arrow labelled benefit runs toward a big crowd standing in front of India's map (138 crore) but is crossed in red; a large red WHY? appears; a green ticked arrow drops from the card to a government icon, which fans out three arrows: healthcare and education get red crosses, defence gets three green ticks

examples.idea: Two reasons the state let private shareholders own the RBI: cost and public trust.
examples.shown_as: the RBI mark stands alone with a 'private shareholders' note; a question mark pops beside it, then two diagonal lines branch down from the note to two red headings - 'financial burden' and 'trust of the public' - each with a paragraph

examples.idea: To fund development, the state wanted control over banks.
examples.shown_as: the timeline slides left; a yellow band starts at 1949 under the words 'focus: economic development' with a factory icon; a bank icon then sends an arrow to the factory (banks fund industry) on a pink strip; a blue circle like a magnifying lens settles over the bank with a callout 'some government control needed', and a box below concludes that a strong nationalised banking system was needed

examples.idea: The biggest bank, the Imperial Bank, was the obvious one to nationalise first.
examples.shown_as: under the 'strong nationalised system' box two reason bullets write on; then they are replaced by a down-arrow to the drawn Imperial Bank building with a note that it led the market with 450+ branches

examples.idea: an investor cannot judge a company's safety alone, so credit rating agencies rate its bonds
examples.shown_as: a factory -> bond -> investor flow with a ? over the investor; under a banner naming rating agencies, a ceiling lamp shines a light cone that widens over the factory-bond box, and a speedometer-style gauge is linked to the bond

examples.idea: banks borrow from the RBI long-term at bank rate and short-term at repo rate; that cost passes into the loan rate people pay, so a lower rate means more borrowing
examples.shown_as: a bank lends to a person by a 'loan' arrow; the RBI emblem above, tagged 'banker of the banks', sends long-term and short-term loans down to the bank; two red % signs labelled bank rate and repo rate sit in a strip and a dotted arrow carries the repo % down onto the person's loan, whose % splits into less (more borrowing) and more (less borrowing)

examples.idea: repo: RBI lends short-term to banks; reverse repo: banks lend short-term back to RBI; RBI sets both and they act on bank liquidity
examples.shown_as: a vertical chain RBI -> short-term loan -> repo % -> bank, and a dotted elbow loop back up from the bank to RBI carrying the reverse repo %; 'determined by RBI' bands over each rate; 'liquidity' under the bank branches to low (red) and high (green) with a definition

examples.idea: repo is a repurchase agreement: the bank gives government securities to the RBI as collateral and promises to buy them back on a set date at a set price
examples.shown_as: the repo chain returns; a bond certificate between bank and RBI links to a government-security label with the national emblem; a dotted loop runs bank -> security -> RBI under a cream band; a checklist agreement document speaks the buy-back promise, with a curved arrow to the bold title 'repurchase agreement'

examples.idea: the RBI buys the security at a discount set by the repo rate; the buy-back price is the rate of repurchase
examples.shown_as: an arrow from the agreement leads to a chain: RBI buys at a discounted price -> worked out from the repo rate -> rate of repurchase; value chips sit on the diagram parts: security worth 100, loan of 100 minus discount

examples.idea: reverse repo: banks park spare funds with the RBI; the RBI gives securities and promises to buy them back (reverse repurchase agreement)
examples.shown_as: the repo chain fades and a dotted loop carries the reverse repo % up from the bank to RBI; a tilted paper note on the bank says banks park surplus funds; a second dotted loop runs RBI -> security -> bank, opposite to repo, under a cream band; the agreement box now highlights 'resell' and is titled reverse repurchase agreement

examples.idea: the government reflates the economy: more public spending, tax cuts and rate cuts push the price level up
examples.shown_as: a dark full-width band slides up from the bottom with one white sentence on the policy response, under the still deflation diagram

examples.idea: a bank's deposits (NDTL) are split: CRR is kept with the RBI as cash earning nothing; SLR is kept by the bank in cash, gold or government securities
examples.shown_as: a bank at the top with NDTL under it splits by red % arrows into CRR 4.5% and SLR 18%; CRR goes to an RBI coin with a gold vault box marked '0% interest', SLR to a grey safe noted cash, gold, SLR securities

examples.idea: the remaining 77.5% is for lending: part is lent and part kept idle in government securities
examples.shown_as: a third branch '77.5% available for lending' rains down-arrows onto a dense crowd of borrower heads; it splits into 'given in loan' and 'kept idle', and the idle part gets a yellow 'invest in government security' box with a certificate and emblem, plus a note that banks earn on SLR

examples.idea: when customers need loans, the bank pledges government securities to the RBI and borrows short-term at the repo rate; repo limits are a share of NDTL
examples.shown_as: a person with a 'Need LOAN' bubble; the bank in the centre with a G-sec certificate; a dotted arrow pledges the G-sec up to RBI, RBI sends a short-term loan through a red repo % down to the bank, and the bank lends on to the person, closing a rectangle loop; green REPO and TERM REPO pills show 0.25% / 0.75% of NDTL

examples.idea: MSF: if loan demand doubles to 40 crore, the bank borrows overnight at the MSF rate by dipping into its SLR, up to 1% of NDTL
examples.shown_as: under an MSF title, loan 20 crore is struck to 40 crore; an orange dotted 'overnight loan' arrow runs from RBI to the bank through a red MSF-rate %, and an orange dotted loop goes from the bank to the SLR safe and back to RBI; the safe swells inside a blue magnifier with 'up to 1% of NDTL'

examples.idea: FPIs invest through the stock market into companies and must register with SEBI
examples.shown_as: a 'foreign investors FPI' box; a stock-exchange tower leads to a factory inside the India box; an elbow 'register' arrow runs from the investor to a SEBI badge sitting on the market

examples.idea: unregistered foreign investors can still invest through registered FPIs using participatory notes
examples.shown_as: foreign investors split into not-registered (person icons) and registered FPI (an institution building), with SEBI badges marked each way; registered FPI -> invest -> market -> company; a light-blue box wraps the not-registered group and a document labelled P NOTE links them

examples.idea: the US dollar was fixed to a set weight of gold, and other currencies were pegged to the dollar
examples.shown_as: gold bars '= X grams' equal a dollar note under a FIXED label; three brown root-like PEGGED arrows run from the dollar to three generic banknotes on a green panel, with short explanations under the panels

examples.idea: a pegged currency moves with its anchor currency; a crawling peg lets it glide within about 1%
examples.shown_as: on value-vs-time axes a dollar note travels along a rising dotted line while a rupee note hangs below it on a rod with a $ pin and moves with it; a yellow +-1% chip at the pin and a 'gliding or crawling peg' label with a definition

examples.idea: an importer pays rupees to a bank and the RBI hands out dollars from its reserves; heavy imports drain reserves into a BoP crisis, solved by devaluation
examples.shown_as: an importer caricature with a brand badge sends a Rs 3.30 lakh note to a bank and on to RBI, with return arrows; a '$1 lakh' dollar note rises out of a forex reserve stack beside the RBI coin; a brace explains the BoP crisis, with a 'solution' line and a pink DEVALUATION pill

examples.idea: WPI is published by DPIIT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (earlier DIPP)
examples.shown_as: a ministry name card with the national emblem is plugged by a cable into a megaphone announcing WPI; dark chips give the department names and an old-name chip with an up-arrow

examples.idea: every account is a two-sided ledger, so each account and each half of the BoP ends up in plus or minus
examples.shown_as: the bullet lists vanish and a small chalkboard with a debit|credit T-chart drops under each of the four leaves; a curved arrow names them double-entry bookkeeping; a down-arrow under each board ends in '+ / -'; then one black frame closes around the two current boards and another around the two capital boards, each frame getting its own +/- result

examples.idea: Agency houses acted as go-betweens who got the Company past the barrier.
examples.shown_as: the challenge notes clear; a teal strip with blue squares slides in between the wall and the merchants; two curved arrows loop from the company over and under the wall into the strip - the agency houses carry the company's business around the obstacle

examples.idea: By lending to merchants and borrowing from the public, both for interest, agency houses became banks.
examples.shown_as: the 'we want' tags clear; a green elbow arrow carries a banknote from the agency house over to the merchant (short-term loan) with a purple up-arrow and % above it for interest; a crowd labelled 'general public' appears below and three green arrows lift banknotes up into the agency house, with % up-arrows beside the crowd (they earn interest too); then the agency house's blue square turns into a yellow box labelled BANK

examples.idea: in the old system each loan rate was settled by bargaining, so stronger borrowers paid less
examples.shown_as: a bank lends to a person along a 'loan' arrow; both get a yellow % tag (bank 15%, person 5%); as the loan amount is struck from 10 lakh to 20 lakh, the bank's tag is struck and rewritten lower again and again (15 -> 12 -> 7 -> 5) until it meets the person's 5%

examples.idea: RBI made banks fix a BPLR and treat it as the floor, expecting clear and uniform loan pricing
examples.shown_as: four bank icons sit in a pink box under the BPLR heading; the RBI coin appears below and four dotted arrows rise from it to the banks, then a red [FIXED] tag lands on the box; beside RBI a wavy brace opens to 'BPLR = minimum interest' and two goal chips

examples.idea: the global answer to bank risk is to make banks keep their own capital as a cushion, measured against their risky assets
examples.shown_as: a dark grey panel slides over the risk list, framed by the BIS mark and Basel I/II/III chips; a brace on the three risks draws a line to a 'capital' tag, which splits into tier I and tier II; under it 'how to decide?' leads to three ratio abbreviations

examples.idea: central banks meet and trade information through BIS, which is a bank only for central banks
examples.shown_as: the BIS mark moves to the centre and five two-headed arrows shoot out to central-bank labels around it; a caption box writes on under the hub, one phrase is highlighted, and a second box adds that BIS banks only for central banks

examples.idea: a committee of central bank governors at BIS writes the Basel rules so world banking stays sound
examples.shown_as: a line from the BIS mark leads to a long committee table with a row of heads behind it; under it 1974 and 'G10 -> central bank governors' write on; a 'developed' arrow runs to 'norms', whose faint label is swapped for a Basel accords tag, and a down-arrow lands on a framed 'sound and stable global banking' goal

examples.idea: the government sells IOUs through the RBI to banks for less than the amount it will pay back
examples.shown_as: on the right, the government emblem hands a certificate to the RBI coin (arrows emblem -> certificate -> RBI); RBI drops the certificate down an arrow into a blue primary-market banner where banks and NBFCs sit; an up-arrow with a small ticked token beside the down-arrow shows payment going up as the certificate goes down; a label says it is sold at a discount and a pointer adds face value 1 lakh, discounted price 90K

examples.idea: buying a bond means lending to a company, so the buyer bears the risk that the company fails to pay
examples.shown_as: a factory labelled XYZ sends a bond certificate along an arrow to investor A on a cream 'corporate bond' strip while a rupee note travels back above on a dotted line; a red RISK disc then drops over A, and a callout line links A to an inset of the same man lying awake, captioned that he fears a default

examples.idea: a CDS shifts the risk of a bond default from the bond holder to the CDS seller
examples.shown_as: a CDS certificate rises on an arrow from a tall office building (seller B) up to investor A, tagged 'Credit Default Swap', with a rule paragraph at the side; then the red RISK disc lifts off A and slides down to sit over B's building, leaving A uncovered

examples.idea: the protection is not free: the buyer pays the seller a regular premium
examples.shown_as: the inset of the wide-awake man is replaced by a dark panel of floating Z's (he now sleeps); a dotted line runs from A down to B carrying a small money icon, with a blue note that A pays a periodic premium for the protection

examples.idea: borrowing in the money market means handing a security into the market and taking cash out of it

examples.idea: a T-bill is a short government IOU sold through the RBI below face value; the gap is the buyer's return

examples.idea: a CD is a bank's tradable short-term deposit receipt sold to the market for cash
examples.shown_as: a bank logo stands over the same down-security / up-cash arrow pair into a pale-green MONEY MARKET box marked 'all'; a blue bar names it [CD] certificate of deposit; a callout gives lot size and minimum, a 7-364 days line appears, then an 'exceptions' badge leads to a second line for all-India financial institutions at 1-3 years with a callout naming them

examples.idea: a bank turns a trade promise into cash today and collects from the buyer later
examples.shown_as: a long arrow carries the bill from the ABC-XYZ line down to the bank; a blue bar labels it [CB] commercial bill, 7-364 days; a cash note rides an elbow arrow from the bank up into ABC's box; finally a second cash note drops from XYZ down to the bank stamped with the due date, closing the loop

examples.idea: repo = selling securities for cash now with a promise to buy them back
examples.shown_as: the T-bill chain flashes back with RBI now holding a coin stack; it narrows to RBI and its money pile above a bank logo that 'needs cash' and holds four certificates; two certificates glow yellow, a 'sell' arrow lifts them up to RBI while a cash note drops to the bank; a blue frame closes around both arrows as one deal and a checklist sheet tagged [REPO] hooks onto it, with a dotted line back to the Repurchase Agreement chip

examples.idea: strong companies borrow short-term from the market by selling their own IOUs
examples.shown_as: the same down-security / up-cash pair now hangs under the words TOP RATED CORPORATES over a pale-green MONEY MARKET box marked 'all except RBI'; a blue bar names it [CP] commercial paper and a callout gives lot size and the 5-lakh minimum

examples.idea: villagers can pool savings into their own bank, but part of the pool must be parked as CRR and SLR before the rest is lent

examples.idea: services flow down the chain: state bank -> district bank -> local societies and town banks
examples.shown_as: the bands vanish and the coloured squares regroup into a vertical tree: SCB at top, a down-arrow marked many to DCCB, which forks to many PCS and many UCB; three tinted note boxes, each in its square's colour, hang off the levels on dotted leader lines

examples.idea: a fixed slice of every bank's deposits must sit as cash with RBI, earning nothing, at a rate RBI chooses within the law
examples.shown_as: bank icon on top with its NDTL label; a red arrow drops to a % sign and runs down into a gold vault held by the RBI coin, marked cash and 0% interest; a law icon writes '3% to 15%' into the % and a blue 'decides' arrow links RBI to it; then an 'Amend 2007' tag sends a dotted arrow that strikes the range and writes 'up to 15%' above it

examples.idea: SLR money stays in the bank's own safe in liquid form, ready for depositors
examples.shown_as: a second red arrow drops from NDTL beside the first, through its own % sign, into a small grey safe labelled SLR that stays with the bank, not with RBI; 'gold, cash or G-secs' writes under it and a callout box explains it as a cushion for withdrawals

examples.idea: holding CRR and SLR is compulsory, checked by RBI every fortnight, with a penalty for a shortfall
examples.shown_as: the bank sits beside a grey 'reserve ratios' card with the vault (CRR) and the safe (SLR); an elbow arc 'maintain - mandatory' arches over it; a report icon tagged fortnightly rises on an arrow to the RBI coin, and a dotted 'penalty' line loops from RBI back down to the bank with a red 'if not maintained' note

examples.idea: Small banks are aimed at specific poor groups within a fixed area.
examples.shown_as: a long crowd fills the right panel and four red circles ring small clusters inside it - the marginalised groups; two small bank buildings appear above and drop dotted lines straight into those circles, so each bank serves its own targeted cluster; the 'targeted approach' item glows in the sidebar menu

examples.idea: Small banks keep costs low by using technology.
examples.shown_as: the text below clears; a dotted ring of small tech icons (tools, search, laptop, shield, server, chat) circles each small bank above the crowd, and 'technology driven' lights up in the sidebar

examples.idea: Small banks can serve both town and village customers.
examples.shown_as: the tech rings clear and the crowd is painted in two halves - grey 'urban' and green 'rural' - with a small bank's dotted lines reaching into both halves; 'flexibility' lights up in the sidebar

examples.idea: A wallet firm passes through an RBI licence and comes out as a payments bank that can hold and move money but cannot lend.

examples.idea: Payments banks are kept away from lending risk, and wallets are not the only ones who can apply.

examples.idea: national income has four measures (GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP); we start with GDP
examples.shown_as: four abbreviations, each joined by a short red dash to its full form, under a NATIONAL INCOME chip; a green band and a tick pick out GDP

examples.idea: both groups contain commercial banks and co-operative banks

examples.idea: the kinds of commercial banks under each group (public, private, foreign, regional rural, small finance, payments, local area)
examples.shown_as: dotted stems drop under each Commercial Banks node and leaf names are added about 1.5 s apart, six on the scheduled side then five on the other, each pointed at by a tiny green arrow

examples.idea: the Monetary Policy Committee has six members: three from the RBI (Governor as chair) and three named by the government

examples.idea: RBI's tools are qualitative (act on liquid money indirectly) or quantitative (act directly)

examples.idea: causes of a short-term disconnect: company news, optimism, global factors, monetary policy

examples.idea: rating scales run from the safest grade down to junk; the grade tells investors the risk of default

examples.idea: GDP can be real (constant prices) or nominal, each at factor cost or market price: four ways
examples.shown_as: GDP -> real / nominal by blue arrows, each splitting into factor cost / market price, under a big red 4 'ways of calculating' heading, with a pointer 'constant prices' on real

examples.idea: price inflation has two causes, cost-push and demand-pull, tied to two schools of thought (Keynesian before the 1970s, Monetarist after)

examples.idea: the general price level can fall (deflation) or rise (inflation)

examples.idea: foreign investors invest in India in two ways: FDI and FPI

examples.idea: RFPIs fall into three risk categories, each with example investor types
examples.shown_as: RFPI -> category I / II / III -> low / medium / high risk, with blue example lists under each

examples.idea: inflation is measured by WPI and CPI; a grandparent's memory of 1000 against today's 5000 shows why prices are compared over time

examples.idea: the WPI basket has 697 goods in three groups: fuel and power 13.15%, manufactured products 64.23%, primary articles 22.62%

examples.idea: many kinds of dealings with other countries move foreign currency and so push the forex reserve up or down

examples.idea: the BoP has two halves; the current half counts goods traded plus services, incomes and gifts/remittances
